stop_rule: Do not further tune King Rail latent-state models on the same response. Move the generated prediction to response-frozen replication.
primary_general_hypothesis: Observed-positive source models exaggerate ecological turnover when true site use is persistent but detection is intermittent; cumulative site history should rescue apparent one-step propagation failures more often than increasing spatial reach alone.

per_species_endpoints.prior_site_fraction: fraction of post-initialization positives at previously detected sites
per_species_endpoints.gap_return_fraction: fraction of post-initialization positives that return at a previously detected site after at least one observed gap

primary_cross_species_prediction.statement: Species with more gap-return/persistent-site structure will show larger rescue when source memory is extended from the immediately previous occasion to cumulative site history.
primary_cross_species_prediction.test: Spearman association across all analyzable species between gap_return_fraction and cumulative_memory_rescue at the broad 17.01-km scale; report all species and leave sparse species non-estimable rather than switching species.

secondary_prediction.statement: After first-positive initialization is removed, broad cumulative history should reduce unsupported positives more consistently than merely interpreting every unsupported detection as long-distance movement.
secondary_prediction.output: species-wise paired table of immediate versus cumulative unsupported positive counts at each fixed scale

claim_boundary: This panel tests detection-history geometry, not true movement routes.
Same-site gap return is compatible with persistence plus imperfect detection but does not prove occupancy.
No alpha-code may be dropped because its result is inconvenient; sparse data are reported as non-estimable.
King Rail is the hypothesis-generating seed and is excluded from prospective cross-species confirmation.
